text:
lin: Heads-up — we're seeing a KV hit drop (~12%) on sessionized traffic after yesterday's runtime patch. Not sure if it's eviction or key mismatch. Any ideas?

marta: yep same. spike in page faults on node pool-rlc-3 around 03:12 UTC. looked like different keys for identical prefixes.

james: I profiled longctx clients — memory growth looks tied to per-request key variants. I can upload a flamegraph later.

sasha: quick check: are we still including request_id in kv key? that would break reuse. :thinking_face: 

lin: nope shouldn't. but the old code path did `fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s:%d", tenant, prefix, seq)` — seq is a session counter, maybe leaked into non-session flows.

anand: also saw a commit that moved normalization earlier but didn't strip trailing whitespace. different prefixes -> different fingerprints.

marta: reproduced locally. two requests with identical text but different trailing newline => different cache keys. hit rate 0 -> 0.83 after normalizing.

james: patch idea: canonicalize prefix, then use a 80-bit fingerprint (murmur3_128 truncated) + model_id + quant_profile in the key namespace so we avoid long unhashed keys. example: 

```
// pseudo
prefixNorm := normalizePrefix(prefix)
f := murmur3_128(prefixNorm)
short := f >> 48 // keep top 80 bits
kvKey := fmt.Sprintf("m:%s:p:%x:q:%s", modelID, short, quantProfile)
```

This keeps key size small and preserves tenant/model separation.

sasha: also we should cap prefix length; hashing full longctx is expensive and prevents prefix coalescing. propose using a rolling window (last 256 tokens) for fingerprinting so common tails still collide.

lin: numbers? what's perf gain expected from this change?

marta: ran a small A/B on canary with canonicalization + 80-bit fingerprint: hit rate improved +9.7 percentage points (62.3% -> 72.0%), P50 generation latency down ~18ms, and mem growth on longctx plateaued on our stress tests. eviction churn decreased noticeably.

anand: two notes: 1) 80-bit collision risk is tiny for our tenant count if we namespace with tenant+model; 2) need to version the key format so we can roll back/invalidate easily (e.g., add `v2` prefix).

james: I also noticed batching heuristics affect reuse — small prefixes coalesced into the same batch increase sharing but the batcher sometimes scrubs model_id when it folds requests. make sure the batch keying includes model_id and key_version.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled to eng-runtime/canary at 2026-03-17T11:40:00Z — user marta — rollout 10%.

sasha: after canary we should add instrumentation: increment `kv_key_normalization_version` tag on hits/misses and emit sample of raw->norm mapping for 1/10000 requests (PII-sanitized) to detect anomalies.

lin: agreed. i'll open a PR with the normalization + fingerprint helper + perf tests and add the metrics. i'll also include a small migration plan for key_versioning so we can toggle. thanks all :thumbsup:

marta: ping me when PR is up, i'll run the longctx mem growth suite.

anand: i'll review the hash impl and sanity-check collision tests.

james: i'll attach the flamegraph and the canary dashboard once deploy is running.

lin: final note: keep the old key parser around for 24h in logs to help with rollback investigation.
